why: Every strategy/risk change invalidates prior data. This window is the first period during which the desk's behaviour is held constant, so the result actually means something.

frozen.strategy_logic: no changes to entries, exits, sizing or the conviction gate
allowed_during_window: genuine bug fixes (wrong, not merely improvable)
observation cadence (CYCLE_MINUTES) -- it changes how often the frozen logic is evaluated, not what it decides; any change must be logged in 'amendments'

evidence.primary: desks/paper (crypto trainer) and desks/stocks — enough trade count for statistics
evidence.secondary: live Robinhood crypto desk — validates real execution, fills and costs
evidence.caveat: The paper trainer runs a looser 0.40 conviction gate than the live desk's 0.52, so its results do not directly predict live behaviour. Conviction is also compressed (the 12-agent average lands in 47-53%), which is why the live desk trades rarely. Recalibrate AFTER this window using the hit-rate-by-conviction data it collects — not before.

success_criteria.primary: net-of-fees return beats buy-and-hold BTC over the window
success_criteria.quality: positive Sharpe on the equity curve
success_criteria.minimum_sample: at least 30 closed trades, else the result is not significant

decision_rule: VOID (see 'voided'): do NOT add capital, do NOT cite this window's P&L as evidence for or against any strategy, and restart only once every restart_precondition holds. The original rule is preserved below for the re-run. Pass on all criteria → scale capital deliberately. Fail, or fewer than 30 trades → do NOT add capital; recalibrate and re-run the window.

amendments.what_it_changes: How often the desk observes the market and re-evaluates, inside an Actions job that runs for DESK_LOOP_MINUTES either way: ~11 cycles per scheduled window instead of ~3. Strategy logic, sizing, the 0.52 conviction gate, the risk ceilings and the fee model are untouched.
amendments.why: The window's own minimum_sample is 30 closed trades. At cycle 456 it had 1 trade in 2.65 days -- on track for an inconclusive result caused by too few decision points, not by the strategies. Making the change at 2.9% elapsed costs far less comparability than discovering the sample shortfall at day 90. It also lets the bar recorder build genuine 5-minute bars (config.bar_intervals_for), which a 15-minute poll cannot.
amendments.cost: More broker and LLM calls per hour, and more status.json commits. No additional Actions minutes.
amendments.comparability: Trades before and after this timestamp are drawn at different observation rates. Report the window's trade count and Sharpe split at this boundary as well as pooled; do not present the pooled figure alone.

voided.verdict: VOID — this window cannot produce a usable out-of-sample result and will not be cited as one
why: The risk gate was broken for the whole window. RiskEngine.approve compared only the incremental order against the per-position cap, so any desk that averaged in compounded past it one approved order at a time; separately, a position the venue could not quote was valued at 0.0 and weighed nothing against the total-deployed cap. Both are fixed (PR #21), but every trade recorded before the fix was sized by a gate that was not enforcing itself.

Both PRIMARY evidence desks are therefore measuring leverage accidents, not strategy. desks/paper is +5.5% while holding EDRY at 62x its per-position cap (621% of equity); desks/stocks is at -$26,414 from the same defect with the sign reversed. Same bug, opposite luck. Neither number is attributable to the strategies under test.

The SECONDARY live desk cannot reach the sample floor. minimum_sample is 30 closed trades; it has 1 in 9.1 days. Extrapolated over the full 90 days that is ~10, and no arrangement of the remaining 81 days changes it, because the binding constraint is council conviction landing in a 40-54% band against a 52% gate.

Both desks also carry position records that contradict themselves (DIA held at -9.935112 shares while recorded 'long'), so direction and realized P&L on those rows are wrong independently of the sizing.
what_this_does_not_mean: The strategies are not disproven by this. They are unmeasured. The window failed as an instrument; it did not return a negative result.
Nothing is deleted. The original protocol, criteria and amendment are kept above exactly as written, so the void is auditable rather than a rewrite.
restart_preconditions: python -m tools.position_audit exits 0 on every desk — no over-cap, unpriceable, contradictory or insolvent position anywhere.
Both paper desks flattened, so the new window starts from a clean book rather than inheriting positions sized by the broken gate.

The conviction gate recalibrated against the hit-rate-by-conviction data Hermes has collected. Doing this is the ONLY change that was forbidden during the window and is now the precondition for the next one: a gate that the conviction distribution almost never crosses cannot generate a sample.
A demonstrated trade rate that reaches 30 closed trades inside 90 days. Measure it over a week before starting the clock, not after.
voided.decided_by: autonomous desk operator, on the evidence above
